method: Independent semantic reviewer judgments on explicit complete answer counterexamples, not a claim that an LLM grader was executed. Vectors are minimum adequate/full-versus-inadequate core decisions for these concrete answers; point calibration within failed answers is reviewer judgment.

construct-tables.A: Temperature measurements. A transposed table has first row Time/h: 0, 1/2, 3/2 and second row Temperature/°C: -3/2, 1/2, -1/2. The third data column means a measured temperature of minus one half degree Celsius after one and a half hours.
construct-tables.B: Club choices. A table has columns Club and Number of people and rows Music 6, Robotics 11, Drama 8. Club names are categories, not physical quantities; the count names people and can be dimensionless.

read-tables.A: The highest recorded temperature is 1.5 °C at 0.5 h. The difference is 1.5-(-2.5)=4 K. The recorded value rises from -2.5 at 0 h to 1.5 at 0.5 h, then falls to -0.5 at 1.5 h. No measurement at 1 h or 3 h is given, so neither temperature is established.
read-tables.B: Two bottles cost EUR4, four cost EUR8; EUR8-EUR4=EUR4. Among those shown pairs the smaller pair has half as many bottles and half the price of the larger pair.

read-diagrams.A: The horizontal axis is time in hours, vertical is temperature in °C. At 0 h the mark is -1/2 °C, and at 1/2 h it is +1/2 °C. Adjacent vertical ticks, e.g. 0 and 0.5, represent half a degree; the first point lies below zero.
read-diagrams.B: Club categories are vertical and number of people is horizontal. Drama corresponds to 6 people, music to 10. The adjacent tick labels 4 and 6 differ by 2 people; the labels drama/music identify categories, not times or measured temperatures.
